title: Production methods
examples: What is the difference between making one item and making many?
When would a factory use automation?
Can you give an example of job production in real life?

explain.say: Today we are learning about different ways things are made.
Job production makes one unique item for one customer.
Batch production makes small groups of identical items.
Flow production makes many identical items continuously.
Automation uses machines to do the work with little human help.
Think about a local bakery making wedding cakes for many different people.

faq.q: What is the main difference between batch and flow production?
faq.a: Batch production makes small groups of similar items, while flow production makes many items one after the other.
asks: When do I use batches versus continuous flow?
Is flow production always for cars?

faq.q: Does automation mean no people are working there?
faq.a: No, automation means machines do the repetitive tasks, but people still manage and fix the machines.
asks: Are humans needed when machines do the work?
What is the role of people in automated factories?

faq.a: Job production can be expensive because each item needs custom design and materials.
asks: Does making something unique cost more?
What affects the cost of job production?

faq.q: Can a factory use more than one method?
faq.a: Yes, many large factories use a mix of methods depending on the product they are making that day.
asks: Can one business use several production types?
Is it normal to mix production methods?

faq.q: Which method is best for making plain pencils?
faq.a: Flow production is usually best for plain pencils because they are identical and need high volume.
asks: What is the best method for simple, common goods?
Should I use job or flow for pencils?

facts: Job production is used when products are highly customized for a single buyer.
Batch production is efficient when making several units of the same product type.
Flow production is best for standardized goods made in very high volumes.
Automation increases speed and consistency but requires high initial setup costs.

quiz.say: A custom-designed wedding dress made by hand for one person is an example of:
quiz.why: Job production is used when making one unique item for one specific customer.

wrong.1: This is wrong because batch production involves making a small group, not just one item.
wrong.2: This is wrong because flow production requires making many identical items continuously.
wrong.3: This is wrong because automation describes the tools used, not the method of making the item.

quiz.say: A factory making 500 identical light bulbs every hour uses:
quiz.why: Flow production is designed for making large quantities of identical items quickly.

wrong.0: This is wrong because automation is the technology, not the method of continuous output.
wrong.2: This is wrong because job production is for single, unique items only.
wrong.3: This is wrong because batch production involves making smaller, defined groups of items.

quiz.say: A company making 20 different flavours of shampoo in groups of 100 bottles each uses:
quiz.why: This describes making distinct, small groups of identical items, which is the definition of batch production.

wrong.0: This is wrong because job production focuses on one single, unique commission.
wrong.1: This is wrong because flow production suggests a single, continuous stream of one type of item.
wrong.2: This is wrong because automation is about machinery, not the grouping strategy itself.
